name: Big Pit: The Old Lodge Workings

signs.title: The Fed
signs.text: THE FED. The South Wales Miners' Federation was founded in 1898, after a lock-out that lasted about six months. Its lodges ran institutes, libraries and medical aid societies that no company would pay for, and a lodge's banner was carried at the front of any march.
A coal tub on rails, and in the floor a plate, rusted but sound. A gate at the far end is held shut by something that wants weight.

gates.line: A timber gate blocks the road, and a plate in the floor looks as if it was meant to lift it.

text: The lodge minute book, damp but legible. The last entry: 'Resolved: that the lodge hall, the library and the baths be held in trust for the men of this valley for as long as there is coal under it, and after.'
The signature underneath is a cross-hatched scrawl and the date is 1936. There is a ring on the page where somebody once put a mug of tea down.
A lodge banner, folded on a shelf. Moth has had the red but the gold lettering holds: UNITY IS STRENGTH.
Banners like this were carried at the head of marches, and nobody carried one for show.
